title: Android TabWidget: invisible tab
purpose: Check that an invisible Android tab keeps its space but cannot be selected by tapping that empty space.
changes: Invisible TabWidget children no longer draw or receive taps; their layout slot is retained. The example adds a switch to hide and restore the middle tab.
steps: Select First, then turn on Hide Second (keep space). Second should disappear while the gap between First and Third stays the same size.
Tap the empty middle space. The selected-tab label should still say First.
Turn the switch off, then tap Second. It should reappear and become selected.
Repeat with Right-to-left layout enabled. Choose OK if it works, or Reject with details and your device.
expected: The hidden tab keeps its space and cannot be selected by tapping; after restoration it can be selected normally in either layout direction.
limits: This checks an invisible XML child; full Android measurement and device visual parity remain unverified. An already-selected tab remains selected when hidden.

references.scope: TabWidget measurement includes invisible children while gone children are excluded.

validation: Eight TabWidget Rust tests passed, including invisible child layout and input in both layout directions.
A 320 × 440 browser interaction test checked the empty slot, restoration and RTL.
